name: brinn-mcp

tools.name: create_entry
tools.description: Captures a new journal entry, thought, or memory. Use this whenever the user shares a new fact, expresses a feeling, or wants to save context about their life for future reflection.

content.description: The main text content of the journal entry.

mood.description: The mood category (e.g., happy, calm, stressed).

tags.description: List of tag names or IDs to categorize the entry.

collectionId.description: Optional ID of a collection to organize this entry into.

tools.name: list_entries
tools.description: Searches, filters, and retrieves past journal entries and memories to gain deep context about the user's history. Use this tool to answer questions like 'What did I think about X?', 'How was my emotional state last week?', or to find specific memories using keywords and semantic search capabilities.

q.description: Optional search query for keyword or semantic search.

mode.description: Search mode. 'deep' uses AI semantic search.

collectionId.description: Filter by a specific collection ID.

tags.description: Filter by one or more tag IDs.

tools.name: read_entry
tools.description: Fetches the full, detailed content of a specific journal entry or memory. Use this tool after discovering an entry ID via list_entries to read the complete reflection, historical context, and any attached metadata.

id.description: The unique ID of the entry to retrieve.

tools.name: update_entry
tools.description: Refines, corrects, or updates an existing journal entry. Use this tool when the user wants to elaborate on a past thought, correct an observation, add missing tags to an old memory, or re-organize a reflection into a different collection.

id.description: The unique ID of the entry to update.

mood.description: The mood category (e.g., happy, calm, stressed).

collectionId.description: Move the entry to a different collection ID.

tools.name: delete_entry
tools.description: Permanently deletes a specific journal entry or memory by its ID. Use this tool only when the user explicitly requests to remove incorrect, sensitive, or redundant information from their Digital Sanctuary.

id.description: The unique ID of the entry to delete.

tools.name: list_collections
tools.description: Retrieves a list of the user's organizational collections (e.g., 'Work', 'Personal Research', 'Daily Logs'). Use this tool to understand the high-level structure of the user's workspace or to identify the correct collection for a new or existing entry.

tools.name: create_collection
tools.description: Creates a new organizational collection (bucket). Use this when the user wants to start a new project, track a new life area, or group their thoughts under a specific category.

name.description: The unique name of the collection.

description.description: A short description of what this collection is for.

color.description: A hex color code for the collection UI (e.g., '#FF5733').

icon.description: An icon identifier or emoji for the collection.

tools.name: read_collection
tools.description: Retrieves the full details and metadata of a specific collection by its ID. Useful for understanding the scope of a project or area of life.

id.description: The unique ID of the collection to retrieve.

tools.name: update_collection
tools.description: Updates an existing collection's details like its name, description, color, or icon. Use this to refine the organization of the user's sanctuary.

id.description: The unique ID of the collection to update.

name.description: The new name for the collection.

tools.name: delete_collection
tools.description: Permanently deletes a specific collection by its ID. CALL THIS ONLY IF THE USER EXPLICITLY ASKED TO DELETE, REMOVE, OR DESTROY A COLLECTION.

id.description: The unique ID of the collection to delete.

tools.name: get_user_tags
tools.description: Retrieves all existing tags used by the user, including their names, colors, and usage counts. Use this tool to discover recurring themes in the user's notes or to ensure that newly created entries use consistent tagging patterns.
